references.text: The same expression 'be cut off from one's people' (וְנִכְרַת) is used as a penalty for failing to bring the offering to the tabernacle
The same penalty of being 'cut off from one's people' applies to anyone who disobeys the Lord's command
The same wording regarding being 'cut off from one's people' is used for violating the Lord's laws
Uses the same expression about being 'cut off' (כרת) as a penalty for sin
The context of the command: the tenth day of the seventh month is the Day of Atonement, when one must fast (ענה)
The same penalty of being 'cut off from one's people' applies to anyone who fails to celebrate Passover
The same penalty of being 'cut off from one's people' applies to anyone who sins willfully
Parallel text concerning the Day of Atonement and the command to fast/humble oneself (ועניתם)
Prophetic teaching on true fasting and humbling oneself (ענה נפש)
Reference to 'the fast' (τὴν νηστείαν) which is the Day of Atonement mentioned in Leviticus 23:29
